title: Reidentify: Context-Aware Identity Generation for Contextual Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

problems.title: Multiplicative logit mask fails unique-identity constraint
problems.source_claim_location: Section4.2 p5 Eq4-5; Eq8 p6; Algorithm1 p13
assumptions: Mask as explicitly defined:0 used,1 unused
problems.check: Analytic positive forbidden mass; exhaustive n2,3,5 zero-logit enumeration
problems.result: All forbidden identities retain positive mass; five-agent zero-logit collision probability0.9616
counterevidence: Conventional additive masking could be implemented despite written formula
Experimental gains and permutation visualization do not establish literal implementation
problems.impact: Invalid defining constraint in specified core algorithm; actual run impact Unverifiable
problems.correction: Mask probabilities and renormalize, or additive negative-infinity logit mask
problems.repair_verification: Local uniqueness proved by induction and enumeration; training not rerun

independent_check.source_fidelity: Freshly viewed physical p.5 Section 4.2: uniqueness is a hard constraint, mask is zero for used labels, Eq.(4) masks before Softmax, Eq.(5) draws from P. Read p.6 Eq.(8) and Appendix A p.13 Algorithm 1 line 13.
independent_check.operative_assumptions: n finite labels for n agents, finite decoder scores, binary mask as defined, categorical Draw. Zero scores are admissible; the stronger positive-forbidden-mass argument holds for every finite score vector.
independent_check.independent_reasoning: A used identity has masked score zero and hence exp(0)=1, yielding strictly positive forbidden mass. At (-5,-5), M=(0,1), repeat probability is 1/(1+exp(-5)). At all-zero scores every conditional draw is uniform on all n labels; independent enumeration matches n!/n^n. Eq.(8) has P-StopGrad(P)=0 in the forward pass, so it cannot restore support. Algorithm 1 explicitly invokes Eq.(8).
independent_check.counterevidence_and_alternatives: A conventional additive minus-infinity mask or explicit unused-index sampling would repair implementation intent, but neither appears in the printed probability formula or Algorithm 1. Finite negative constants only approximate a hard zero. Permutation visualizations and empirical gains do not identify the executed code.
independent_check.dependency_and_severity: Major for the defining uniqueness constraint in the specified core autoregressive assignment algorithm. No measured collision rate or empirical learning failure is inferred for the unavailable implementation.
independent_check.repair_scope: M_j exp(h_j) normalized over nonempty unused labels gives exactly zero used-label mass. Induction over a=1,...,n ensures n-a+1 choices before each step and a final permutation. Only support correctness is restored, not gradient estimator properties or learning performance.

repair_verification: Local identity support corrected and verified; implementation unavailable
